key_insight: A mixed s0/d0/d10 high-entropy perovskite electrolyte, (Ba0.50Sr0.50)(Ti0.33Zr0.33Sn0.33)O3, outperforms two related compositions by combining low leakage, low ohmic resistance, and strong ion-conduction behavior.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a rare-earth-free electrolyte design route for solid oxide fuel cells that can improve performance while expanding the materials palette for durable, high-temperature devices.
method: Synthesized three high-entropy perovskite electrolytes via sequential sintering, high-pressure torsion processing, and calcination.
Printed ~6–10 μm electrolyte films on Ni-SrZr0.5Ce0.4Y0.1O3 anodes and coated them with Ba0.5La0.5CoO3 cathodes.
Evaluated electrochemical performance using impedance spectroscopy plus synchrotron X-ray absorption and photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: The (Ba0.50Sr0.50)(Ti0.33Zr0.33Sn0.33)O3 electrolyte achieved the best reported performance, with negligible current leakage, the lowest ohmic resistance, and a maximum power density of 0.53 W·cm-2 at 973 K.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated at high temperature and on a specific cell architecture, so scalability, long-term stability, and manufacturability still need validation.
paper_title: High-entropy perovskites, architectured by s0/d0/d10 cations, as novel electrolytes for solid oxide fuel cells
